subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Hightower Retail / embeddings + rerank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Hightower Retail / embeddings + rerank

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet today, and thanks for walking us through Hightower's search/rerank plans. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps. Let me know if I missed anything or if you'd like this split into a shorter MAP.

Pain points / goals we heard:
- Current product search is brittle for new/seasonal SKUs; relevance drifts with catalog churn.
- Rerank layer (TF-IDF + business rules) gives inconsistent UX across categories (apparel vs. home).
- Latency constraints: product detail / list pages need p95 end-to-end <=250ms; search rerank portion target p95 <=120-150ms.
- Cost sensitivity: team wants per-query incremental cost to be affordable at 1M+ queries/month (target ~<$0.02/query).

Current stack (what you told us):
- Metadata + catalog: Postgres (primary) + S3 for assets.
- Vector DB: Pinecone (single-region) for embeddings, currently storing ~45M vectors (256-d) with HNSW indexes.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for product titles/descriptions today; generating embeddings at write-time (batch nightly + real-time for new SKUs).
- Frontend: client issues search request -> candidate generator -> rerank via embedding similarity + business scoring.

Workload profile / scale:
- Index size: ~45M product vectors, growing ~3-5M vectors/month (peak catalog seasons).
- QPS: baseline 40 QPS, peak 150 QPS during promo windows; majority of traffic is read/serve (hot) with bursts.
- Index update pattern: nightly bulk ingestion for catalog sync (~3-5M vectors), plus streaming updates (hundreds/hr) for new SKUs and price changes.
- Query pattern: mix of single-query user searches and batched analytics reruns for personalization (batch inference jobs run overnight).

Success criteria for a POC we agreed on:
1) Accuracy: recall@10 improvement over baseline >= +0.10 (relative) or absolute recall@10 >= 0.85 on provided eval set.
2) Latency: p95 retrieve+rerank <=150ms for single-item queries (end-to-end of embedding similarity & rerank tuning).
3) Cost: estimated per-query cost <= $0.02 at 1M QPS/month equivalent (include compute + vector DB ops).
4) Operational: support incremental updates with <5s visibility for new embeddings in the hot index, and graceful degradation to a lightweight model when load spikes.

Redwood POC proposal / next steps:
- PoC dataset: 10M-vector sample (we recommend starting with a geographically representative slice including top categories and seasonal SKUs).
- Setup: Redwood will provide a temporary dedicated endpoint + config (HNSW settings, quantization profile) and a small benchmark harness to run both latency and recall tests.
- Timeline: 2-3 week PoC (week 1: ingest + baseline run, week 2: tuning + rerank experiments, week 3: validation + handoff).
- Deliverables: benchmark report (latency/cost/quality), suggested production config (batching, quantization, cache strategy), and an initial MAP.

Action items we agreed on:
- Hightower: share sample dataset (10M vectors), evaluation queries, and baseline metrics (recall@10, current p95).
- Hightower: confirm compliance/security reqs (SOC2, data residency) and whether Pinecone must remain in the loop.
- Redwood: send MAP + PoC tech checklist and quote for a 3-week dedicated PoC.

Attachments: Hightower discovery notes & MAP (attached).

Possible meeting slots for kickoff next week: Wed 10/21 10:00-11:00am PT, Thu 10/22 9:00-10:00am PT. Which works for you?

Thanks —

We'd like to target Thu 10/22 9-10am PT for kickoff if that slot's still available. Looking forward to the MAP and quote.

Alex — appreciated. We've updated the MAP to reflect canonical index size (~38M) and the slightly tighter p95 target for the rerank stage (<=120ms). Attached is the MAP + PoC tech checklist.

Quick notes on approach given what you shared:
- Sampling: we'll create the 10M slice balanced across top 5 categories + 30% tail SKUs to stress test cold vectors.
- Caching: propose a hot-warm cache strategy — keep top 5M vectors in a low-latency quantized cache for <50ms lookups; rest served from optimized index. This helps hit p95 while controlling cost.
- Quantization: recommend 8-bit quantization with asymmetric quant scales for product image/text combos; reduces storage and speeds inner-product ops without large quality hit.
- Batching: online queries should stay single-query synchronous; large personalization reruns can use Redwood's batch workers to amortize embedding compute overnight.

Attached: Hightower-MAP-20261020.xlsx (has milestones & success criteria).

Confirming kickoff Thu 10/22 9:00-10:00am PT. I'll send a calendar invite. For the PoC we'll need your sample export (10M vectors) and the eval query set by EOD Fri 10/23.

Next internal ask — Vivek / Neha: can you review the MAP & tech checklist and confirm resource needs (dedicated endpoint size, expected cpu/gpu footprint for 10M ingest) so I can include an estimated quote in the kickoff pack?

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the note and MAP. Quick engineering read: 
- For a 10M ingest test with 256-d vectors, a single NVIDIA A10/A100 slice with Redwood's ingest pipeline should handle initial ingestion in ~6-8 hours with streaming normalization; recommend provisioning 2x A10 for faster turnaround during PoC.
- Endpoint sizing: to meet p95 <=120ms for rerank (hot 5M cache + rest in optimized index), we should provision 2 dedicated inference workers (8 GPUs worth of serving capacity across 2 nodes) and enable prefix KV caching at the route level.
- Cost estimate (PoC): ~USD 6,500 for the 3-week dedicated environment (compute + storage + engineer support). Will formalize and send a short quote.

I'll sync with Neha on SRE/CS handoffs.
